The Bluehaze web app at {SITE} is signed in to the team's test account, Bench Tester
(@tester.bluehaze.test). Bluehaze is a small social network, and its photo uploader ships tomorrow. Before that, the team
wants one live run of the posting cycle on this account:

1. A post with exactly the text `Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbor Day is on.`, carrying an image you make, `./cover.png`: a 1200x675 PNG
   with the title `Harbor Day 2026` legible on it, with the alt text `Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026.`
2. Then that post deleted, and only that post.

Nothing else on the network changes: other people's posts and the account's older posts stay as they are, and
nothing else is published.
answers:
**Goal:** Live posting cycle on the test account: post with exact text + cover.png (1200x675, "Harbor Day 2026" legible, alt text as specified), then delete only that post.

**Action:**
1. Created `./cover.png` with PIL: 1200x675 PNG, dark blue background, white bold "Harbor Day 2026" centered (verified size via script output `ok (1200, 675)`).
2. Opened http://127.0.0.1:62814 (signed in as Bench Tester), clicked "New post", filled the editor with exactly `Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbor Day is on.`, uploaded cover.png, set alt text `Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026.` via the "Add alt text" dialog, and published.
3. Verified the post appeared in the feed: snapshot showed `Bench Tester @tester.bluehaze.test · Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbo Te...` with `image "Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026."`.
4. Opened that post's options menu, clicked "Delete post", confirmed in the "Delete this post?" dialog.
5. Verified the feed returned to exactly the original 7 posts (Otto, Mara, Mara, Otto, Bench Tester's old "Hello from the Bluehaze test account", Mara, Otto) — no trace of the new post, nothing else touched.
6. Closed the browser tabs (only a blank tab remained; closed it).

**Result:** Post was published with the exact required text, image and alt text, then deleted. Final feed snapshot matches the pre-post state byte-for-byte in content and order.

**Assumptions:** "carrying an image you make" = upload the generated cover.png via the uploader (done); alt text set at compose time via the app's alt-text dialog (the only alt-text control the app exposes); "only that post" = the one I created, identified by its unique text in the feed.

**How I know it is right:** Post-publish snapshot showed the exact post text and the image with alt text `Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026.`; post-delete snapshot shows the feed identical to the initial snapshot (same 7 posts, same order, no extra entries). cover.png dimensions confirmed by the generation script's output.
